## Registration
- `POST /fcm/register-token` (`src/fcm/fcm.controller.ts:30-49`) is protected by `JwtAuthGuard`. It takes the user id from `@CurrentUser()` and the body `RegisterDeviceTokenDto` (`deviceId`, `fcmToken`).
- `FcmService.registerDeviceToken` (`src/fcm/fcm.service.ts:91-120`) allows only one active token per user:
  - If the user has any existing row, it calls `unregisterAllDeviceTokens` (`:146-151`). That soft-deactivates every row by setting `isActive=false` and `deletedAt=now`.
  - It then inserts a new row (`:106-112`).
  - Any failure is rethrown as `BadRequestException`.
- `DELETE /fcm/unregister-token/:deviceId` (`fcm.controller.ts:51-66`) calls `unregisterDeviceToken` (`fcm.service.ts:127-140`). That deactivates the row for that `userId` and `deviceId`.

## Storage
- The `DeviceToken` entity is in `src/fcm/entities/device-token.entity.ts:11-39`. The table is `device_tokens`.
- Columns: uuid `id`, `user_id`, `device_id`, `fcm_token` (text), `is_active` (default true), `created_at`, `updated_at` and `deleted_at`.
- Indexes: `user_id`, `device_id`, and a composite `(userId, isActive)` (`:12`).
- Related migrations are `1753262876986-add-device-token-table.ts` and `1754380262420-update-device-tokens-tables.ts`.

## Sending
- Firebase Admin is initialized in the `FcmService` constructor (`fcm.service.ts:39-83`). It parses the `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_KEY` env JSON and fixes the `\n` escapes in the private key.
  - If the key is missing, it only logs a warning (`:47-52`). `firebaseApp` stays unset, so later sends throw "Firebase service not available" (`:238-241`).
- `sendNotificationToUser` (`:172-195`) does the following:
  - It looks up the single active token via `getUserDeviceToken` (`:158-164`).
  - If there is none, it logs a warning and returns `{success:false}`.
  - Otherwise it calls `sendNotificationToToken` (`:234-277`).
- `sendNotificationToToken` sends a **data-only** message, `{token, data}`, with `firebaseApp.messaging().send` (`:255-260`). There is no `notification` payload.
- `removeInvalidTokens` (`:283`) is private and never called, so stale tokens are never cleaned up on FCM errors.

## Callers
- `calls.service.ts:114` sends the incoming-call push (`sendCallingNotificationToUser`, `fcm.service.ts:305`, event `INCOMING_CALL`).
- `in-call-notification.service.ts:100` sends the missed-call push (`fcm.service.ts:326`).
- `vouched.service.ts:245` sends the KYC-passed push (`fcm.service.ts:203`). A failed KYC sends nothing.
- `POST /fcm/send-to-user/:userId` (`fcm.controller.ts:68-81`) is an admin endpoint behind `RolesGuard`.
- `auth.service.ts:230, 273, 501` read the token with `getDeviceTokenByUserId` (`fcm.service.ts:292`), presumably to return it in the user and guest profile responses. I didn't open those lines.
